transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Samira Patel (Redwood SE); Diego Ramos (Redwood Infra); Laura Kim (NexaHealth ML Eng); Marcus Boone (NexaHealth CTO); Priya Singh (Data Lead); Tom H. (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Weekly quantization check-in. Reviewed INT8 vs FP8 runs from last week, noted small BLEU/ROUGE-like regressions on conversational evals at 99% confidence for some tails. Performance: INT8 shows 1.8-2.2x token/sec improvement on A100, FP8 shows 2.4x but with increased instability on long contexts on H100 with current runtime kernel. Action: longer regressions, share benchmark sheet, infra follow-up.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - uh quick roll call, we have, Samira, Diego from our side, and from Nexa Health Laura, Marcus, Priya, Tom. Can you confirm?
[00:12] Laura Kim: Yep, all good here. Thanks Alex.
[00:15] Marcus Boone: Morning. Quick note, we're time boxed to about 45, hope that's okay.
[00:20] Alex Chen: Yep that's perfect. We'll focus on the quant results first then blockers and next steps.

[00:35] Samira Patel: Alright so I pulled together the latest runs - we've got INT8 per-channel calib, and FP8 experimental runs. Quick recap: test suite is our 2k prompt eval set (mix of convo, summarization, and extraction tests), measurements at seq len 512 and 2k for tail behavior.
[01:05] Priya Singh: Just to confirm, the 2k prompt suite includes PII redaction cases - we masked those in the shared data, right?
[01:12] Samira Patel: Yes, we used the masked copy - and logs are redacted. The raw data never left Nexa's cluster.

[01:30] Tom H.: Cool. So results: INT8 had about a 1.8x throughput increase on A100 when compared to FP16 baseline, and latency p50 improved similarly. FP8 was showing about 2.3-2.4x on average on H100, but we did see instability on a subset of long-context prompts.
[02:05] Laura Kim: When you say instability, do you mean crashes or quality drift?
[02:10] Samira Patel: More quality drift - generation divergence on follow-up prompts, and occasional tokenization mismatches in the post-processing. Not full crashes, but samples failing regression thresholds.
[02:28] Marcus Boone: Did you try per-channel vs per-tensor calibration for INT8? We saw per-tensor earlier and that had weird spikes.
[02:36] Samira Patel: Yes, we re-ran with per-channel - that tightened the tails, reduced regression delta from ~3.5% to ~1.1% on the conversational BLEU-like metric. But some edge-case extraction tasks still show small drops.

[03:00] Diego Ramos: On the infra side, we noticed H100 runs have variance depending on driver/kernel combo - the throughput numbers fluctuate ~10% across different CUDA versions. We're digging into possible cuDNN kernel selection differences.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Can that explain the FP8 instability?
[03:23] Diego Ramos: Possibly. FP8 kernels are newer, and small differences in tensor core scheduling or kernel fusion could amplify numeric noise, especially with long KV cache sequences.

[03:40] Alex Chen: Ok that matches our lab repros. Samira, do you have the per-prompt breakdown? Any particular buckets where FP8 fails more?
[03:52] Samira Patel: Yes - FP8 shows higher regressions on the multi-turn context summarization and code completion-ish prompts. Simpler Q&A tasks trend fine. I can share the CSV. There's also an odd tokenization mismatch on a subset of Spanish prompts - looks like a pre-tokenizer edge case.
[04:20] Laura Kim: Huh interesting. We do run a slightly different tokenizer pre-step internally, could be related. We'll double-check.
[04:30] Marcus Boone: From a decision standpoint, if INT8 gives ~2x throughput with only ~1% quality loss on average, that seems attractive. FP8 faster but with some instability; might be risky in prod. Thoughts?
[04:46] Alex Chen: That's the tradeoff. For user-facing latencies and safety we recommend starting with INT8 with per-channel calib for production, and FP8 for batch or non-critical workloads until we stabilize kernels and tokenization.
[05:05] Samira Patel: Agreed. Also cost estimates: on A100 INT8 mode reduces token cost by ~42% vs FP16; FP8 shows ~52% reduction but with variance. I'll attach a per-million-token cost row in the sheet.

[05:30] Tom H.: Can you remind - are KV cache behaviors preserved exactly in INT8? Any difference in memory footprint?
[05:36] Samira Patel: Yes KV cache preserved; memory footprint drops because int8 activations are half size of fp16, so you get ~40-45% mem reduction which helps batch size. But note fp8 uses different packing and can be slightly more compact on some kernels which is why we saw the bigger throughput boost on H100.

[06:05] Priya Singh: Regression thresholds - what are we using? The same as before?
[06:09] Alex Chen: We used your baseline thresholds in the shared eval config - overall pass/fail at 95% of baseline. But we also flagged per-task deltas.
[06:20] Priya Singh: Ok we care more about extraction accuracy and PII redaction conservation, so let's prioritize those metrics.

[06:40] Samira Patel: Note on calibration: INT8 per-channel required a small calibration dataset - we used 5k tokens sampled from your corpus. If you prefer we can re-run with a customer-specific calibration set you provide, might reduce the edge-case drops.
[06:56] Laura Kim: We'll prep a sanitized calibration set - maybe 2k examples focused on extraction and redaction.
[07:03] Marcus Boone: Any security concerns about calibration data? We don't want to leak internal examples.
[07:07] Alex Chen: We recommend uploading to your S3 in the VPC or sharing via our private bundle; Redwood won't persist plain-text calibration data and logs are redacted per our process. We can do an SFTP if you prefer.

[07:30] Diego Ramos: Back to infra - one more thing, we saw a couple of OOMs on the A100 when running mixed-batch with 2k sequences at INT8 + large batch sizes. Might need to tune micro-batching or KV sharding.
[07:46] Tom H.: That's likely because our current request shaping assumes fp16 mem footprint. Good catch.

[08:00] Alex Chen: Let's go over the specific numbers in the sheet - Samira, could you summarize the key rows?
[08:07] Samira Patel: Sure: baseline FP16 p50 latency at seq512: 95ms; INT8 p50: 52ms; FP8 p50: 39ms. Throughput (tokens/sec) baseline: 18k; INT8: 33k; FP8: 44k on H100. For A100 FP8 was closer to 36k (less headroom). Regression average delta across suite: INT8 1.1% drop, FP8 2.9% but with 0.6% of prompts failing critical extraction thresholds.
[09:00] Laura Kim: That 0.6% failing extraction is a bit concerning if it's deterministic on some prompts. Are they clusterable?
[09:08] Samira Patel: They cluster around long context with nested list extraction and some Spanish tokens. We're seeing tokenization edge-case plus numeric noise compounding on long KV cache.
[09:24] Marcus Boone: Ok statistically small but operationally risk-y. Our users run compliance workflows; false negatives are bad.
[09:31] Alex Chen: Right - our recommendation: start with INT8 per-channel for prod, enable FP8 for internal batch jobs and continue kernel stabilization. Also run a nightly regression for INT8 and flag any new failures.

[09:55] Priya Singh: For the nightly run, what infra footprint do we need? Can we run it in our existing cluster?
[10:00] Diego Ramos: Yes, we can provide a lightweight runner image; but watch batch sizes to avoid OOMs. We'll send recommended configs.
[10:08] Tom H.: Also please include the exact CUDA/cuDNN version you used so we can match.
[10:14] Samira Patel: Of course - we'll include per-run metadata: CUDA 12.2 / cuDNN 9.0 in the sheet for H100 runs, and CUDA 11.8 for A100 runs.

[10:30] Alex Chen: Any legal or security items to note this week?
[10:34] Marcus Boone: We just need to confirm logs are redacted and calibration data handling. Also want to know if any model weights get uploaded.
[10:42] Alex Chen: No weights leave your VPC. Calibration artifacts are aggregated stats, not raw tokens, unless you explicitly share them. We'll document that in the follow-up email.

[10:55] Samira Patel: Quick ask - can Nexa run the FP8 stability test on a small H100 node overnight while we iterate? If you can, send us the logs and we'll triage the tokenization issue.
[11:05] Laura Kim: We can do one H100 rack tonight and run the FP8 long-context suite, yes.
[11:11] Alex Chen: Great. OK last bit - decisions and next steps recap.

[11:20] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) Move forward with INT8 per-channel as the candidate for production testing; 2) Nexa to run regression suite overnight on INT8 and FP8 and upload artifacts; 3) Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet, cost rows, and exact run metadata (CUDA/cuDNN) today; 4) Infra deep-dive scheduled next Tue (Diego + Nexa infra) to look at H100 kernel variance; 5) Samira to push INT8 per-channel config to shared S3 path.
[11:55] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Please include target dates in the email.
[12:00] Alex Chen: Yep - I'll send an email after this. Anything else?
[12:05] Marcus Boone: No, thanks everyone.

[12:10] Alex Chen: Thanks all.

End transcript.
